about.heading: Who is *Profal Kumar?*
paragraphs: I'm pursuing my Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering at **Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET)**, majoring in Structural Engineering with a minor in Water Resources Engineering.

I like technology and solving problems. I've designed multi-storied reinforced concrete buildings in ETABS and AutoCAD, modelled flood risk with HEC-RAS, simulated traffic in PTV Vissim, and used Python machine learning for engineering forecasting.
I'm looking for challenging work where I can contribute to an organisation's growth while building my technical and communication skills.

items.title: Holcim HQ Dhaka: "The Breathing Ring"
items.summary: Category 3 (Next Generation Visionary Design) entry: a five-storey corporate headquarters built as an open ring crossed by twin office wings. I designed the structure and the sustainability strategy.
bullets: Reinforced-concrete dual system of special moment frames and 12" shear walls at the lift and stair cores, plus six radial walls. Modelled in ETABS 22 to BNBC 2020 and ACI 318-19.
Seismic drift of 0.0018 against a 0.020 limit, and 100% of members pass. Design base shear is 2,080 kip.
A 127.6 kWp rooftop solar system avoids about 108 t of CO₂ per year, and rainwater harvesting collects about 3 million litres per year. The design also uses low-clinker cement.
items.image_alt: 3D render of Holcim HQ Dhaka: a curved five-storey office ring with orange facade screens, green terraces and solar carports

items.kind: Data Science · GCI World 2026 Final Assignment
items.title: The Quiet Goodbye: Predicting Customer Churn
items.summary: Proof of concept for a US telecom company (Company A): a Python machine-learning model that spots customers who are about to leave, and a retention plan that only spends money where it pays back.
bullets: Analysed 100,000 customers and found a 1-year cliff: churn jumps from 29% at month 9 to 65% at month 11, when contracts end. Old phones and falling usage are the other warning signs.
Compared three models in scikit-learn. Gradient Boosting ranked customers best, with ROC-AUC 0.699 on 20,000 customers it never saw.
The model's riskiest 10% churn at 81%, against 19% for its safest 10%, and every score comes with a reason and a matching offer.
Designed a targeted offer program, stress-tested it, and planned a 90-day pilot with a control group before any scale-up.

items.title: Spatio-Temporal Prediction of Coastal Embankment Failure in Sundarbans: An Integrating Remote Sensing, Hydrodynamic and Machine Learning Approach
items.authors: **P. Kumar***, N. Roy and M. A. Sayeed
items.affiliation: Department of Civil Engineering, RUET · *Corresponding author
items.summary: Combines Landsat land-cover mapping, mangrove-based Manning's roughness, a HEC-RAS 2D model of the 31 March 2025 Bichhat breach, and machine learning to study coastal embankment failure in Assasuni, Kaliganj and Shyamnagar (Satkhira).

stats.label: AUC for predicting failure-level tide days
RMSE, next-day water level (40% better than persistence)

method: Classified land use and land cover for 2000, 2010, 2015 and 2025 from Landsat imagery with Random Forest in ArcGIS Pro.
Turned land-cover classes into spatially varying Manning's n values for the HEC-RAS 2D model, driven by BWDB tide data from station SW26.

Labelled 885 embankment segments (500 m each) from 44 dated breach records (2007–2026), then trained logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting models with spatial block cross-validation.
Built a preliminary embankment susceptibility map to help prioritise monitoring and mangrove protection.

items.title: Thermal Performance Enhancement of Asphalt Pavements Using Polymer-Modified Bitumen: A Bangladesh Perspective
items.authors: Tanbir Ahmmed, **Profal Kumar** and Md. Abu Sayeed
items.summary: Evaluates polymer-modified bitumen (PMB) as a binder for Bangladesh's hot, wet climate, where conventional 60/70 bitumen (softening point only 45–52 °C) leads to rutting, thermal cracking and deformation. The study aims to find the best polymer type and dosage and to give implementation recommendations for the national highway network.

stats.label: Bangladesh road network the study targets

method: Modify base bitumen with different polymers at 5%, 7% and 9% by weight, using high-shear mixing at 180 °C.
Test specimens to ASTM standards: penetration (D5), softening point (D36), ductility (D113) and viscosity (D4402).
Use a Dynamic Shear Rheometer (DSR) to assess viscoelastic behaviour and rutting resistance against Superpave requirements.
Compare life-cycle cost, service life and carbon emissions of PMB with conventional bitumen.

founder.heading: Founder of *Kumar Math*
paragraphs: I started **Kumar Math** in 2023 to help HSC and university admission students in Bangladesh learn Higher Math, Physics and Chemistry the clear way: step by step, formula by formula.

The **Kumar Math HSC app** brings it together in Bangla: chapter-wise lectures and formula lists for every Physics and Chemistry chapter, MCQ practice with explanations, and a study routine. I also write admission model tests with answer keys.
